'''Cecil Wilfrid Luscombe''' "'''Bill'''" '''Bevan''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRSA}} (2 April 1920 – 19 April 1989) was a Welsh [[chemist]], academic, and [[academic administrator]]. He was [[Principal (academia)|Principal]] of [[University College, Cardiff]] from 1966 to 1987. He was additionally [[Vice-Chancellor]] of the [[University of Wales]] for two terms: 1973 to 1975 and 1981 to 1983.<ref name="WWW">'BEVAN, Cecil Wilfrid Luscombe', ''[[Who Was Who]]'', A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 1920–2016; online edn, Oxford University Press, 2014; online edn, April 2014 [http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whowaswho/U161987 accessed 31 Aug 2017]</ref>

==Academic career==
Bevan worked at the [[University of Exeter]] from 1949 to 1953, before moving to the [[University of Ibadan]] in Nigeria. He was head of its Department of Chemistry from 1953 and 1966, and its Vice Principal and [[Deputy Vice-Chancellor]] from 1960 to 1964.<ref name="WWW" />

==Honours==
In the [[1965 New Year Honours]], Bevan was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE).<ref name="LG 43529">{{London Gazette |issue= 43529 |date= 29 December 1964 |page= 20 |supp= y }}</ref> He was made an officer of the ''[[Ordre des Palmes Académiques]]'' by the government of France in 1986.<ref name="WWW" />

In 1969, Bevan was made a [[Honorary fellow|Fellow]] of [[University College London]] (UCL);<ref name="WWW" /> this is an honorary appointment recognising "distinction in the arts, literature, science, business or public life".<ref>{{cite web|title=Honorary Fellows of UCL|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/srs/governance-and-committees/committees/hdfc/honorary-fellows/#b|website=Student and Registry Services|publisher=University College London|accessdate=31 August 2017|archive-date=20 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120215645/https://www.ucl.ac.uk/srs/governance-and-committees/committees/hdfc/honorary-fellows#b|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1971, he was elected as fellow of the [[Royal Society of Arts]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mercer |first=George Edward |date=1971 |title=Notices of the Society |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41370801 |journal=Journal of the Royal Society of Arts |volume=119 |issue=5181 |pages=571–586 |issn=0035-9114}}</ref> He was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary]] [[Doctor of Science]] (DSc) degree in 1973 by the [[University of Ibadan]].<ref name="WWW" /> In 1982, he was made an Honorary Fellow of [[University College, Cardiff]].<ref name="WWW" />
